stories.title: US midterms set to deliver verdict on Trump presidency
stories.summary: In the United States, millions of voters are heading to the polls today as the final day of voting gets underway in the midterm elections. The outcome will determine which party controls Congress for the second half of Donald Trump's presidency. Republicans are defending their record in power over the last two years while Democrats are hoping to turn voter frustration into electoral gains Polling suggests Democrats are well positioned to win control of the House but the battle for the Senate is tighter. Republicans losing the House would give Democrats the power to stall Mr Trump's legislative agenda and launch sweeping investigations of his administration. A Senate defeat would also threaten his ability to appoint Supreme Court judges and senior officials.

stories.title: Apple forecasts margin drop as rising memory costs bite
stories.summary: Apple has warned that the cost of memory chips would continue to rise, pressuring gross margin for the crucial Christmas quarter, but said it had taken steps to lock in supplies. Shares, little changed in after-hours trading after fiscal fourth-quarter results beat expectations, fell 4% during a conference call after executives outlined the weaker outlook, but later pared losses to a 2% decline. Early demand for the iPhone 18 Pro lineup and higher prices boosted the quarter. Apple said it expects gross margin of 45% to 46% in the quarter ending in December, down from 47.9% in the fourth quarter. It forecast services revenue growth of 8% to 9%, below analysts' expectations of 10.7%. The results come as Apple experiments with a string of firsts under new CEO John Ternus, who took over in September. After nearly two decades of launching most new iPhones each autumn, Apple this year is spacing them out, with iPhone Pro and Duo models shipping this year and other models expected next year. Apple also released a bevy of new non-iPhone products this quarter, including its first touchscreen laptops and first smart-home hub. The steady drumbeat of releases, analysts said, is meant to smooth out Apple's yearly revenue cycle, which for decades showed a huge holiday-quarter boom that petered out by late summer.

stories.title: Point of Law wins Melbourne Cup as Maher sweeps top three
stories.summary: Point Of Law won the Lexus Melbourne Gold Cup as Ciaron Maher trained the first three home. Sons And Lovers was the first of Joseph O'Brien’s five-strong contingent to finish, coming home in fourth place. James J Braddock finished back in seventh place, as Maher claimed the other five slots in the top seven, Having claimed the Bahrain Trophy at Newmarket in July for John and Thady Gosden in the colours of the King and Queen, Point Of Law was bought privately by Wathnan Racing. In winning the Geelong Cup on his first start for Maher, he was immediately promoted to favouritism and came in at 11/2 with Ethan Brown on board. Point Of Law was made to work for victory by Royal Supremacy, who at one stage led by 15 lengths before fading in the final furlong.

stories.title: John Malkovich: 'Nobody liked my Irish accent!'
stories.summary: Actor John Malkovich has joked about how his attempt at an Irish accent in his new movie Wild Horse Nine fell flat with Irish members of the film crew and director Martin McDonagh. Set shortly before the 1973 Chilean coup, the film by the In Bruges and Banshees of Inisherin writer and film maker sees Malkovich play Chris Carlisle, a jaded CIA agent who takes a break from destabilising the Chilean government and is dispatched to Easter Island with his partner Lee Chesterfield (Sam Rockwell). This odd couple spend most of the time driving around in a battered old coupe (the coup comes later) and bickering as they visit the island's famous monolithic statues while discussing the nature of the dirty work they carry out on behalf of the US government. Chris, who is also riddled with Catholic guilt and terminal cancer, is seeking to salve his conscious after a lifetime of covert activity by writing his tell-all memoirs. As he says to Lee at one point, "I was killing people before you were born." Meanwhile, back in the Chilean capital of Santiago, Steve Buscemi as bureau chief MJ is slowly losing his mind as he worries that lose cannon Chris is about to betray everyone. It’s classic McDonagh stuff. Quirky and absurd, what seems like a classic shaggy dog story sees the Anglo-Irish director riff on recurrent themes such as stunted morality, guilt, redemption, and men’s basic inability to communicate with each other.

stories.title: Twixmas travel: Where to go to escape the chaos of Christmas
stories.summary: Communications Consultant and Travel Enthusiast Lisa Regan shares her travel ideas for breaking up the 'Twixmas' period by taking a break to cities like Paris, Copenhagen, Tallinn or London. Listen back above. For many of us, the hustle and bustle of Christmas is all part of the charm, while for others it is potentially the most overwhelming time of the year. Regan is one of those people, and for the last few years she has been jetting off to destinations like Costa Rica, Mexico and Panama to escape the carnage. "I always go futher afield", she tells Brendan O'Connor. "It's just not my time to shine, I'm not into Christmas so I like to go [somewhere] warm and just get a total break from everything that's going on and all the shopping and all the antics." She recalls that when she first started going abroad for Christmas there was "a lot of questioning as to why". "It seemed a bit groundbreaking, but I think throughout the years more and more people have dipped their toe to try it themselves or they've heard of more people doing it so now I don't seem as out there when I'm travelling at Christmas time." Even if Christmas seems like your favourite time of year, Regan suggests trying it some year: "It really is a lovely time to go and it breaks away from a lot of the stress and those obligations that sometimes are put on ourselves and then obviously in the family way as well too.

stories.title: How often do you need to clean your solar panels?
stories.summary: Analysis: The cleaning requirements will vary based on the season, house location, orientation and size and angle of the installation Solar panels are a low maintenance solution for domestic sustainable energy production. Once your solar photovoltaic installation is complete, the only point of failure is the electrical equipment, which should last as per the manufacturers' guarantee. However, the maintenance or cleaning of the panels need to be considered. No two solar installations are the same so the cleaning requirements will vary based on the season, location, orientation and size/angle of the installation. Any contamination on the outside of your externally mounted solar panels will impact electrical efficiency by blocking the sunlight from activating the photovoltaic material. Consideration should be given to future cleaning of the solar panels at the time of installation with the solar panel installer as part of the future maintenance. As a significant amount of domestic solar photovoltaic panel installations are installed on the roofs of two-storey buildings, a means of roof access will be needed at some stage. It may require a specialist cleaning service with mechanically or electrically operated platform lift or scaffold. Any contamination on the surface of the panels will still allow the photovoltaic panel installation to operate, but it will reduce efficiency and by default this will increase the payback period and reduce any potential saving on electrical energy costs. Regular solar panel cleaning is a worthwhile investment in your renewable energy system's performance and longevity. In Ireland’s climate, where rain, wind, and agricultural activities can impact panel efficiency, maintaining clean panels helps ensure optimal energy generation throughout the year. The house location and surroundings will have the largest impact on the frequency of cleaning requirements. Urban environments generally require less cleaning because of the lower variance of airborne contaminants, dust, pollen from hedges/grassland and agriculture but having a roadside or private trees which may have some impact.

stories.title: Rovers' O'Neill: Cancer doesn't pick and choose
stories.summary: Shamrock Rovers' Gary O'Neill, who was diagnosed with cancer in October of 2025 and got the all clear earlier this year, has encouraged people to go for regular check-ups in light of his own diagnosis and the recent passing of Ciara Mageean. "When I got diagnosed in October, I tried to keep things as private as I possibly could and deal with whatever was going to come with just me and my family. I didn't really want it to get out. I didn't want the sympathy from people," he said. "It was just about facing my battle with the people I wanted to face the battle with. Then when I got the news that my cancer was shrinking and the treatment was working I became more open to the idea of potentially having a conversation about it. "I thought it was just a really important message for me to spread because I was fit, I was healthy, 29/30 years of age and trained every day. Looked after myself the best I can and I had an 18cm tumor in my stomach when I found the cancer. So, it doesn't pick and choose. It's something that was heavy and if it could have helped one person me opening up my story then I think it's a great success. "My message is and always has been that if something feels off, even if you feel as healthy as you can, there's no repercussions of going to get a blood test. Just go and get yourself checked if you haven't in a while. It's worthwhile just going and doing it now and staying on top of things. These things can be caught early and it makes all the difference." O'Neill added that since receiving his diagnosis and going through treatment, his perspective on things has changed a lot.

stories.title: Stacey Solomon says media intrusion 'should be illegal'
stories.summary: TV presenter Stacey Solomon has said she sometimes feels as though she is being "stalked" by the media, describing the intrusion into her family's private life as "outrageous". The 37-year-old said photographers had waited outside her home and followed her family to events, insisting that some of the behaviour "should be illegal". Speaking ahead of the return of her BBC reality series Stacey & Joe, Solomon said she accepted that being in the public eye came with a certain level of scrutiny, but believed boundaries were being crossed. "I think for a long time in celebrity culture, there was this expectation that you put yourself in the public eye so you deserve this treatment," she said. "If me and Joe go out in the public and there happens to be somebody there and they get a picture of us, that’s fair game. "That’s part and parcel of this industry. We do draw the line though."

stories.title: 8 ways to fix your erratic sleep schedule
stories.summary: New research suggests that an irregular bedtime could have implications for your heart health. Researchers analysed sleep data from more than 10,000 adults who wore activity-tracking devices as part of the National Institutes of Health’s All of Us research programme. The findings revealed that variations in sleep timing from one night to the next over a six-month period were associated with a 20-23% increased risk of serious cardiovascular problems, including heart attacks, strokes and heart failure. Meanwhile, a greater number of complete sleep cycles each night was associated with a 28% lower risk of atrial arrhythmia, a common type of irregular heartbeat. However, unusually long sleep cycles were linked to a 55% higher risk of heart attack or stroke. With growing evidence highlighting the importance of consistent sleep habits, we spoke to Adele Crow, clinical lead occupational therapist at Cygnet Health Care, who shared her expert advice on how to get an erratic sleep schedule back on track. "Try and stick to a realistic time to wake up every day that works for you," advises Crow. "We all have an internal body clock, called a circadian rhythm, and if you’re getting up at a regular time each day that will train your internal body clock.

stories.title: Ryanair passenger numbers rise by 1% in October
stories.summary: Ryanair has today reported a 1% increase in passenger numbers for October as it operated over 109,100 flights during the month. The airline - Europe's largest in terms of passenger numbers - said it carried a total of 19.4 million passengers last night, up from 19.2 million the same time last year. Its load factor - how many seats it fills on each flight - was unchanged at 93%. The airline expects to carry 214 million passengers in its current fiscal year, up 3% from 2025/26. Ryanair yesterday said it was reviewing all its costs due to higher fuel prices and may require staff to take temporary pay freezes after reporting a 15% decline in net profit for the six months to the end of September. It said that while it expects short-haul airfares to rise materially next year, that is unlikely to fully offset an estimated €2 billion increase in its fuel bill for the financial year that ends in March 2028, based on current forward prices.

stories.title: Carbery talk could escalate faster than we thought
stories.summary: Injury issues mean we will see changes in Andy Farrell's team selection for Ireland's Nations Championship test against Argentina on Friday night at Aviva Stadium. Caelan Doris and Jack Crowley remain out, Jack Conan has been added to the injury list after sustaining a shoulder injury with Leinster, and Garry Ringrose is the latest key player to join the list of absentees, leaving Farrell with some important selection decisions. These calls may also give some insight into the longer-term strategy for the team. Leinster centre Ringrose's unavailability is one of the major talking points, particularly when it comes to deciding who will fill the gap in midfield. Bundee Aki and Robbie Henshaw have both played there in the past, but if Farrell wants to establish a more permanent position for Jamie Osborne, Ringrose’s absence could provide another opportunity to develop Ireland’s options at centre. Jamie Benson would be more surprising selection at outside centre, though he has featured there for Ulster. He could provide another playmaking option and help to increase the pace of the attacking game.

stories.title: Funeral to be held for Irish athletics star Ciara Mageean
stories.summary: The funeral is to be held for Irish Olympian and European champion runner Ciara Mageean, who died on Sunday, aged 34. Ms Mageean, from Portaferry in Co Down, competed at the Rio 2016 and Tokyo 2020 Olympics and held multiple Irish records, including in the 800m, 1500m and mile. She won European 1500m gold in Rome in 2024, becoming just the second athlete after Sonia O'Sullivan to secure an individual European title for Ireland. In 2025, she revealed she had been diagnosed with stage-four bowel cancer. She married her long-time partner, Thomas Moran, at a ceremony in Co Louth just weeks before her death. Her funeral service will take place in her hometown of Portaferry at St Patrick's Church at 2pm this afternoon.

stories.title: Primark-Penneys owner forecasts further profit decline
stories.summary: Associated British Foods has today forecast another profit decline this year after reporting a 14% fall in 2025/26, as deeper sugar losses and lower underlying sales at its Primark fashion chain weighed on earnings. The FTSE 100 group, which confirmed in April it would demerge Primark from its food businesses next year, made adjusted operating profit of £1.508 billion for its year to September 12, 2026, on group revenue down 1% on a constant currency basis to £19.58 billion. "In 2027, the group is expected to deliver adjusted operating profit and adjusted EPS below 2026, mainly due to Sugar, as previously guided," the group, which also owns grocery, ingredients and agriculture businesses said. stories.title: 12 properties to rent within HAP limits in September
stories.summary: Only 12 properties were available to rent within any of the Housing Assistance Payment (HAP) Scheme limits in September, according to a new report. The latest Simon Communities of Ireland's Locked Out of the Market report found 1,361 properties were available to rent at any price within the 16 areas surveyed over three dates surveyed that month. That was an increase of 58 properties (4%) since June 2026 and an increase of 528 properties (63%) since September 2025. The publication is the third Locked Out of the Market report conducted under the new legislative framework (Residential Tenancies (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2026), which has seen new tenancies operate on six-year cycles since 1 March. Of the 16 study areas, 11 had no properties available within HAP limits in September. These were: Athlone, Cork city centre, Cork city suburbs, Galway city suburbs, Galway city centre, Co Leitrim, Limerick city suburbs, Limerick city centre, Sligo town, Portlaoise, and Waterford city centre. Four of the 16 areas saw a reduction in the number of HAP properties available since the June 2026 report. These included: Dublin city north (eight properties), Dublin city south (one property), Dublin city centre (one property) and Kildare (one property).

stories.title: Fitzmaurice era begins in Galway, Fallon in backroom team
stories.summary: The Éamonn Fitzmaurice era has offcially begun out west after Galway confirmed the Kerryman has been ratified on a three-year term, with Lisa Fallon part of his backroom team. News broke at the end of September that the former Kingdom boss would succeed Pádraic Joyce. Fitzmaurice won three All-Irelands as a player, and managed Kerry to Sam Maguire glory in 2014. He also claimed six straight Munster SFC titles and an Allianz League during his time in charge. He was part of the Football Review Committee chaired by Jim Gavin. At a county board meeting on Monday night, the appointment was rubber-stamped, as was Fitzmaurice's coaching ticket. UEFA Pro Licence holder Fallon has an eclectic and extensive coaching background. She has worked in soccer with Galway United, Cork City and Chelsea. She was in with the Dublin footballers back in 2018, when they won the All-Ireland SFC title under Gavin.

stories.title: North Korea calls FBI's Binance hack allegations 'absurd'
stories.summary: North Korea has denied the FBI's allegations it was behind the theft of $6 billion from cryptocurrency platform Binance, as it test-fired strategic cruise missiles in a new display of its weapons capabilities. The missile launch came on the heels of a public rebuttal from Kim Yo-jong, the powerful sister of leader Kim Jong-un, who slammed the FBI's allegations as a "grave political provocation". On Saturday, the FBI said a North Korea-affiliated hacking group called TraderTraitor had been behind the hack. Experts see the incident as potentially the largest cryptocurrency theft in history, with a haul equalling "nearly a quarter of the DPRK's estimated annual GDP," Michael Bosack, founding director of the Parley Policy Institute and a former UN Command official, told journalists. Ms Kim said the FBI's claim was "absurd rhetoric and nothing new," given prior US allegations that Pyongyang was behind last year's major hack of Bybit. "The FBI is trying to brand the DPRK as a 'cyber criminal state,' claiming that it obtained information that a hacking organisation 'supported' by the DPRK was involved in the incident," KCNA quoted her as saying.

stories.title: Russia hits Ukraine with heavy strikes as ceasefire ends
stories.summary: Russia has struck Ukraine in overnight attacks, Ukrainian authorities said, as a flare-up in fighting dashed hopes of progress towards peace in the nearly five-year war. The strikes hit areas across the country, killing dozens of people, forcing patients to evacuate a medical facility and triggering a wave of ballistic missile alerts. In Russia, Moscow mayor Sergei Sobyanin said nearly 500 drones heading towards the capital region were destroyed. The attacks followed a rare pause in the fighting between Russia and Ukraine in the southern Ukrainian region of Kherson, which ended Sunday. The truce, which was the longest in the war that erupted in February 2022, enabled a humanitarian mission to the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky. Hours after the local ceasefire ended, Russia targeted a village in Zaporizhzhia in southeastern Ukraine, killing at least 26 people, the acting regional governor said.

stories.title: Butt labels Martinez 'a bluffer' after red at Chelsea
stories.summary: Former Manchester United midfielder Nicky Butt fumed at Lisandro Martinez after he was sent off during his side's 2-0 defeat at Chelsea on Saturday. Butt called the Argentinian as a "bluffer" and a "cheat" for picking up two yellow cards in 83 seconds, including one for an inexplicable elbow on Wesley Fofana. United's latest defeat leaves the club languishing just outside the relegation zone and with head coach Michael Carrick seemingly on the verge of the sack. Butt told the Football Uncensored podcast: "That lad's a bluffer full stop. Performance-wise he's been lacking so much. "He threw it in with that elbow, because that was the most obvious thing anyone could do. The reason he did it is because he's not strong enough to go and defend properly, so you know what? I'll cut corners, I'll cheat and I'll put my elbow in someone's face and I'll get sent off." The Red Devils head into Tuesday's Champions League game against Roma without a win in their last nine matches, which equates to the club's worst run since 1984.

stories.title: US strikes Iranian island ahead of midterm elections
stories.summary: The US has carried out strikes on an Iranian island in ⁠the Strait of Hormuz, according to a US official, hours after President Donald Trump signalled diplomatic progress with Tehran. The strikes, first reported by The Wall Street Journal, hit Qeshm Island, where Iranian state media reported five explosions in rapid succession. Unnamed US officials cited by the Journal and other outlets described the attacks as defensive in nature, while the paper said it was just the latest of several undeclared strikes. It said they had not been publicly announced to avoid the impression the US intended to resume major combat operations. US Central Command did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The US, alongside Israel, launched the war with a massive wave of surprise strikes on Iran in late February, but it has not achieved its war aims and the conflict has been stalemated for months. The strikes come a day before the US midterm elections, with Democrats poised to seize the House of Representatives and challenge for control of the Senate.

stories.title: Barry grabs only goal as Everton defeat 10-man Newcastle
stories.summary: Thierno Barry's second-half strike helped Everton return to winning ways in the Premier League with a 1-0 victory over Newcastle at St James’ Park. Following a first half lacking in clear-cut opportunities, the Toffees took the lead shortly after the restart when Barry stabbed home his fourth league goal of the campaign. A frustrating night soured further for the Magpies as they finished the game with 10 men when substitute Jacob Ramsey was shown two yellow cards in quick succession at the death. Everton ended a three-game winless run in the Premier League, while Newcastle slip to 13th in the table. Monday’s match took place just four days after Everton’s 3-1 win over Newcastle in the fourth round of the Carabao Cup and both sides made two changes to their starting XI as Anthony Elanga and Joelinton came in for the Magpies, while Jarrad Branthwaite and Harrison Armstrong lined up for the visitors. Harvey Barnes looked lively on the left flank for the hosts, sending a curling shot wide before his looping cross floated narrowly past the far post and Jordan Pickford was forced to hold Will Osula's deflected cross from a tight angle.

stories.summary: Weather conditions are a "major" focus of an investigation into a plane crash in Florida that killed nine people, US transportation investigators said. Authorities have not released their identities, saying genetic analysis is needed. US media identified the co-pilot as 20-year-old Nathalia Gadelha Filgeiras, who had received her pilot's license at age 17. stories.title: Protest against citizenship changes to take place
stories.summary: Supporters of migrants will protest outside Leinster House today as the Justice Committee meets for the first time to consider proposed changes to citizenship. If enacted, the Irish Nationality and Citizenship (Amendment) Bill 2026 will increase the standard residency requirement for naturalisation from five to eight years. The General Scheme of the bill also seeks to introduce wealth conditions, mandatory language testing, and an Irish civics exam. The Migrant Rights Centre Ireland (MRCI) and other human rights groups have described it as "cruel" and restrictive. Under the proposals, applicants face disqualification from citizenship if they have received prescribed social welfare payments or state housing supports, such as the Housing Assistance Payment (HAP), in the two years prior to or during their application. There is concern that the bill will send a damaging message to the migrant workers 'propping up' essential Irish sectors.

stories.title: Call for deinstitutionalisation plan for disabled people
stories.summary: The National Advocacy Service (NAS) has called on the Government and the HSE to develop a new national deinstitutionalisation delivery plan. It follows an examination by the NAS of the lived experiences and quality of life of people with disabilities who remain in institutional care. Ireland made a commitment in 2011 to move away from congregated settings. However, a social policy paper issued by the advocacy service today says housing shortages, insufficient community supports, workforce challenges and competing political priorities have impeded progress. In July this year, 1,889 people were living in disability-congregated registered settings, according to the report. In addition, 1,128 younger people with disabilities under the age of 65 currently reside in nursing homes. 108 of them were supported by the National Advocacy Service last year. The report says that people living in these institutions experience a near total loss of autonomy, limited personal control, and separation from the wider community.

stories.title: Coleman 'still thinking about' staying on with Ireland
stories.summary: Séamus Coleman is still keeping the door open on a return to action at club and international level. The 38-year-old, currently without a club, was not included in Heimir Hallgrimsson's UEFA Nations League squad for the quartet of matches in September and October. The indications at the time were that Coleman was on the lookout for a new club in order to prolong his chances of being involved at Euro 2028. Hallgrimsson has shared how keen he is on keeping Coleman in his plans. However the former Everton captain's comments in recent weeks have cast doubt on that possibility. Last week in conversation with Jamie Carragher on the The Overlap Fan Debate, Coleman hinted that he was leaning towards retirement, saying: "I don't want to completely draw a line in the sand, as I said I've been keeping fit. But it's edging towards that way - and happily as well." On Monday, Coleman appeared as a pundit for Sky Sports' coverage of Newcastle United v Everton with speculation rife that he was about to confirm his retirement. Instead, he underlined his stance that nothing has been decided.

stories.title: Carla Lockhart resigns from DUP after Drumcree dispute
stories.summary: Upper Bann MP Carla Lockhart has announced she has resigned from the DUP over its handling of the fallout from the Drumcree parading dispute, and is to sit as an independent unionist in the House of Commons. Carla Lockhart's resignation was widely expected after a clash with the DUP leadership over its failure to remove Sinn Féin's Michelle O'Neill from her role as First Minister. Ms Lockhart believes Ms O'Neill can no longer serve as First Minister due to her participation in a protest the PSNI deemed unlawful against an Orange Order Drumcree parade in Portadown last month. Ms O'Neill and several of her party colleagues are being investigated by police for taking part in the protest on the Garvaghy Road that was staged to prevent the parade proceeding through the predominantly nationalist area. Watch: Northern Editor Vincent Kearney analyses Carla Lockhart's resignation from the DUP The MP had called on her party to withdraw its deputy First Minister Emma Little-Pengelly from her office - a move that would automatically force Ms O'Neill from her role.

stories.title: Ex-rugby international pleads not guilty to perfume theft
stories.summary: Former Irish rugby international Brendan Mullin has pleaded not guilty to stealing a high-end fragrance from Brown Thomas on Dublin's Grafton Street. The ex-rugby player, who won 55 Irish caps between 1984 and 1995 before moving into financial services, is accused of the theft of Hermès perfume worth €158 on 15 May last. He faced his fifth hearing on this charge when he appeared before Judge John Hughes at Dublin District Court. Mr Mullin, aged 62, represented himself because of the ongoing legal aid reform dispute which has led many solicitors to withdraw from District Court cases.
